text.p: Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, which on Friday reported higher third-quarter earnings, said it expected unprecedented financial results for the full year.
"We had an excellent quarter and look forward to record financial results for the year," CanOxy president and chief executive David Hentschel said in a statement.
"But even more encouraging is the steady stream of excellent new projects brought forward by the divisions."
The company earlier reported third-quarter earnings of C$46 million or C$0.34 per share.
That was a 29 percent jump from $38 million or C$0.29 a share reported in the same period last year.
Cash flow in the period grew 29 percent to a record C$189 million or C$1.39 a share.

CanOxy said crude oil production averaged 139,000 barrels a day in the third quarter, up from 134,000 in 1995. Natural gas output increased to 242 million cubic feet a day from 194 million in the third quarter of 1995.

The company said its North American division made considerable progress in the quarter by exploiting its core areas in western Canada and the Gulf of Mexico, as well as making key property acquisitions.
It said it drilled two successful exploration wells and nine development wells on its west-central Saskatchewan joint venture lands, in which it holds a 50 percent interest.
The company also boosted its natural gas exposure in the period by acquiring 156,000 undeveloped acres in Saskatchewan.
In the United States, CanOxy unit CXY Energy is increasing its asset base in the shallow offshore Gulf of Mexico.

The company signed a letter of intent to acquire 100-percent interest in four blocks in the Vermilion area for US$50 million. The blocks contain two fields currently producing 29 million cubic feet of gas and 325 barrels of oil and gas liquids per day.

CanOxy's international division entered into a new production sharing agreement on the Seram Block in Indonesia and acquired a 50-percent stake in a joint venture with Colombia's national oil company to explore the Troyano Block in the Putumayo Basin.
In Yemen, the company's Sunah-10 appraisal well encountered 38 feet of net oil pay in the Qishn zone and another 37 feet of pay in the Shuqra.
It said about 90 square km of 3D seismic would be acquired in the fourth quarter to identify more Shuqra zone appraisal wells.
CanOxy said its chemicals division also showed strong results because of improving demand and several plant expansions.
